# Devplane

> A local-first control plane for AI coding agents. One Rust binary that shows what needs a person across every project on a machine, watches the coding-agent sessions already running, drives any agent speaking the Agent Client Protocol, runs the project's own checks before anything is called done, and writes every decision to an append-only log that names the rule or check behind it. No account, no cloud relay, loopback only.

The unit is a **Work** — the branch, the gates, the pull request, the cost — which outlives the session that started it. **Devplane never approves a tool call**: it can prohibit one and defer one to a person, and grants belong in the agent's own settings.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/quickstart/): install, connect a provider, reach a populated board.
- [Install](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/install/): prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows; the shell installer; building from source.
- [CLI reference](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/cli/): every command, its flags, its exit codes and its `--json` shape.

## Commands

Every command takes a global `--json` that prints machine-readable output instead of a table. Exit codes: `0` success, non-zero on error; `devplane check` exits non-zero when the configuration is unusable.

- `devplane serve`: run the daemon in the foreground.
- `devplane ls` (alias `ps`): sessions in play, and anything asking for a person.
- `devplane inbox`: only what needs a human, most urgent first.
- `devplane issues`, `devplane prs`: every open GitHub issue or pull request across every registered project.
- `devplane show <run>`: one run in detail — state, cost, context, what its checks said.
- `devplane tail <run>`: follow what a driven agent is saying.
- `devplane search <query>`: tool calls, questions and errors across every session.
- `devplane rewind <run>`: files a shell command named for writing, which Claude Code's own `/rewind` checkpoint does not restore.
- `devplane audit`: what Devplane decided, and on whose authority.
- `devplane attention`: whether the inbox is worth reading, per kind.
- `devplane focus <run>`, `devplane attach <run>`: raise the editor window that owns a run, or attach a terminal to it.
- `devplane dispatch`: start an agent on a project with something to do.
- `devplane say <run>`, `devplane decide <run>`: send a prompt to, or answer a permission from, a driven run.
- `devplane agents`: the agents Devplane can drive.
- `devplane check [path]`: read the repository's `devplane.toml` and say what it will do. Offline, daemon-free, CI-safe.
- `devplane explain <call>`: whether the rules refuse or defer one call, and why. `--replay` asks it of every call already observed and composes the grant to paste into the agent's settings.
- `devplane trust [path]`: allow agents to start in a repository, after printing its hooks, MCP servers, skills and overbroad rules. `--dry-run` prints and trusts nothing.
- `devplane work start|list|show|verify|approve|retry|resume|finish`: work that outlives a session, with the project's gates between steps. `--spec <file-or-folder>` names the specification it answers; no format is learned.
- `devplane snooze <id>`: hide a run's inbox items for a while.
- `devplane open`, `devplane watch`: the board in a browser; events as they arrive.
- `devplane doctor` (alias `diagnostics`): channel health, provider, daemon status, and how far a running session has moved past the release the rules were measured against.
- `devplane connect <provider>`, `devplane disconnect <provider>`: install or remove hooks and telemetry, with a backup.
- `devplane stop`: stop the running daemon.
- `devplane mcp`: serve Devplane's read-only surface to an agent over MCP on stdio — `inbox`, `work`, `explain`, `audit`. No tool on it writes; anything that acts still goes through a person. Register it with your agent as a command MCP server.
- `devplane hook`, `devplane statusline`: read a payload on stdin and forward it. Used by the installed hooks, not typed by a person.

## Configuration

- [Configuration reference](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/configuration/): the full `devplane.toml` — `[gates]`, `[pipelines]`, `[policy]`, `[budget]`, `[workspace]`, `[github]`, `[transcripts]`. Devplane reads these files and never writes them; `devplane check --json` and the board's `,` panel print one back.
- [Permissions](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/permissions/): the rule syntax, which is Claude Code's own; `never_auto` and `always_ask`; deny wins in both directions; what a rule cannot see. Devplane never approves, so there is no allow list.
- [Verified done](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/verified-done/): gates, the done certificate, and why an agent's own report is not one.
- [Pipelines](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/pipelines/): declared chains of runs with gates between them, including spec-driven drift checking and `--spec`, which stamps the specification a piece of work answers and counts its task list per gate.

## How it works

- [Architecture](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/architecture/): one binary, two stores, an event log reduced to state, an append-only decision log.
- [Observing](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/observe/): hooks, OpenTelemetry, the agent roster, the optional status-line shim.
- [Security](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/security/): the trust gate, loopback-only, where the policy can and cannot fail open, telemetry privacy.
- [Agents](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/agents/): driving any ACP agent; the four built in and how to name another.

## Optional

- [Decisions](https://hupe1980.github.io/devplane/docs/decisions/): the decision log, what it records and what it deliberately does not.
